newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour calls for crunch vote against minister.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour calls for crunch vote against minister.

text.p: The British opposition Labour party decided on Wednesday to table a censure motion against Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg, a move which could signal an imminent attempt to topple the government.

Labour's senior spokesmen, known as the shadow cabinet, decided to table the motion on Monday. The motion calls for a 1,000 pound cut in Hogg's salary, a parliamentary device to signal no confidence in his handling of the mad cow crisis.
If the ruling Conservatives are defeated in Monday's vote, it would almost certainly prompt Labour to table a no-confidence motion in the government, probably for later in the week.
But a Labour spokesman cautioned the last time a censure motion against a minister was successful was 102 years ago.
Prime Minister John Major's ruling Conservatives are currently tied with all the opposition parties in parliament, although it has 51 seats more than Labour.

But if Labour wins the backing of its fellow opposition parties, many of whom are angry at the continued European export ban on British beef and the government's handling of the mad cow crisis, Major would have to ensure that all his members of parliament, including even sick MPs, turn up for the vote.
With an election due in no more than three months, and Labour well ahead in opinion polls, Major's position is precarious and speculation about the election is rife.
The chairman of Britain's ruling Conservative Party refused on Wednesday to be drawn into the frenzied media speculation.
"Whenever the Prime Minister announces a date, we will be ready," Brian Mawhinney told a news conference at the party's London headquarters.
British newspapers said on Wednesday that Prime Minister John Major would have to make up his mind this week if he wants to call a snap election on March 20.
This would enable Major to avoid a parliamentary by-election going ahead on February 27 in the north-west constituency of Wirral South.
Two opinion polls have suggested that the Conservatives are set for a morale-sapping defeat by the opposition Labour Party in the seat, which they won easily at the 1992 general election.
Major himself has suggested his favoured date for a 1997 general election in May 1. The latest possible date is May 22. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
